result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers quote the specific duplicate values and give a sensible plan: audit, then scales, then tokens, then migration, then lint. A explicitly maps each existing value onto its proposed scale, which shows what will visibly shift. It also keeps the modal as a separate overlay elevation and hedges its contrast estimate and its chunk-only counts. B is slightly tighter and adds useful time estimates and lint rule names, but it calls the modal shadow a one-off instead of a possibly intentional elevation. It also says less about the limits of seeing only one excerpt. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same near-duplicate colors, radii, control heights and spacing from the CSS, and both give a sensible audit, tokens, migrate, lint order. B is better: it maps each existing value onto a target scale, says plainly that small visible shifts will happen, and keeps the overlay elevation separate instead of flattening it. B also hedges its contrast estimate and states that its counts come from this chunk only. A is tighter and easier to scan, but it is less specific about the mappings and about which differences might be intentional.
